```{r Problem text}
#| include: false

# The sentence for one finding is the rule's template from the string
# resources with the finding's values interpolated — one generic path for
# every rule, driven by the context fields `neoipcr::validate()` records
# (documented in its "Context fields" section) and the `{named}` placeholders
# of `content/_sR.yaml`, which use the same names.

# One finding's values as the named character scalars the templates take.
# Dates take the locale's date format; a missing value reads as the report's
# `missing_value` string — worded to sit inside a sentence — so a template
# never receives an NA. Text is escaped for Markdown here, at the boundary:
# a free-text pathogen name or a procedure description is whatever someone
# typed, and must render as that rather than as emphasis, a link or HTML.
format_context <- function(context, sR) {
  if (is.null(context) || ncol(context) == 0L)
    return(list())
  lapply(as.list(context), function(column) {
    value <- column[[1]]
    if (length(value) != 1L || is.na(value))
      return(sR$missing_value)
    if (inherits(value, "Date") || inherits(value, "POSIXt"))
      return(format(value, format = "%x"))
    # Every numeric a rule records is a count of days or an index, so it takes
    # the reports' integer formatting and its locale's digit grouping.
    if (is.numeric(value) && value == round(value))
      return(format_integer(value, big_mark = sR$digit_group_separator))
    if (is.numeric(value))
      return(format(value))
    escape_markdown(as.character(value))
  })
}

# The values a rule's template needs beyond the fields the rule records: the
# localized label of an SSI's infection type (rule 19). The label is looked
# up on the raw value, so a missing or unknown type falls back to the
# missing-value string itself rather than dropping the placeholder's value,
# which would abort the interpolation.
decorate_context <- function(rule_id, values, context, sR) {
  if (rule_id == 19L) {
    label <- sR$ssi_types[[as.character(context$infection_type)]]
    values$ssi_type <- if (is.null(label)) sR$missing_value else label
  }
  values
}

# The template one finding is rendered with: the rule's `description`, or
# for rule 20 its second complete sentence for a pathogen recorded as causing
# a secondary sepsis, rather than one sentence with an optional fragment.
# `_setup.qmd` has checked that every rule carries the templates it renders
# with before anything is composed.
select_template <- function(rule_id, context, sR) {
  key <- if (rule_id == 20L && isTRUE(context$secondary_bsi))
    "description_secondary_bsi"
  else
    "description"
  sR$problems[[as.character(rule_id)]][[key]]
}

# The problem-detail section a rule's finding refers the reader to.
problem_primary_detail <- function(rule_id)
  problem_info$primaryDetail[problem_info$id == rule_id]

# The bullet for one finding: the rule's sentence with the finding's values,
# followed by the cross-reference to the problem's explanation.
problem_text <- function(rule_id, context, sR) {
  values <- decorate_context(rule_id, format_context(context, sR), context, sR)
  sentence <- do.call(
    interpolate_translation,
    c(list(select_template(rule_id, context, sR)), values))
  reference <- interpolate_translation(
    sR$see_problem_details,
    reference = paste0("@sec-problem-details-", problem_primary_detail(rule_id)))
  paste0("* ", sentence, " ", reference)
}
```
